## Natural history notes

A tiny oak gall wasp characterized by a minute, dark wasp-like body, though it is usually noticed through the galls it forms rather than by the adult insect itself. In Florida, Trigonaspis polita is associated with oaks, with records including galls on Chapman’s oak, and is most likely encountered in scrub, sandhill, oak woodland, and other habitats where suitable native oaks occur. The larvae develop inside plant galls induced on oak tissue, where the gall provides both food and shelter; like other cynipid gall wasps, it is harmless to people and forms part of a specialized food web that includes parasitoid wasps and other gall-associated insects.
